system_prompt: You are an expert computational medicinal chemist. Always respond with valid JSON containing a 'modifications' list. Each modification must include 'description', 'smiles', and 'rationale' fields.

modifications.description: Introduction of a guanidinium group to improve ionic interactions with neuraminidase active site residues
modifications.rationale: Replacing the acetamido group with a guanidinium group enhances binding potency by forming stronger ionic and hydrogen bonding interactions with negatively charged residues in the neuraminidase active site, such as glutamate or aspartate.

modifications.description: Addition of a hydroxyl group to the ethyl side chain to improve hydrogen bonding potential
modifications.rationale: Introducing a hydroxyl group to the ethyl side chain allows for additional hydrogen bonding interactions with the neuraminidase active site, potentially increasing binding affinity.

modifications.description: Substitution of the ethyl ester with a cyclopropyl ester to enhance hydrophobic interactions
modifications.rationale: Replacing the ethyl ester with a bulkier cyclopropyl ester increases hydrophobic interactions with nonpolar regions of the neuraminidase binding pocket, enhancing selectivity and binding strength.

modifications.description: Incorporation of a fluorine atom on the cyclohexene ring to improve lipophilicity and binding affinity
modifications.rationale: Introducing a fluorine atom on the cyclohexene ring increases lipophilicity and can improve binding interactions by modulating electronic properties and enhancing fit within the neuraminidase active site.

modifications.description: Replacement of the ethoxy group with a methoxy group to reduce steric hindrance and improve binding
modifications.rationale: Reducing the size of the alkoxy group helps minimize steric clashes with the active site residues, potentially enhancing binding affinity and selectivity.
